sourceDate.text: 幼事葛從周（及壯事梁太祖之前）

units.zh: 楊師厚
units.en: Yang Shihou
units.literal: Yang Shihou

units.zh: 楊師厚，潁州斤溝人也。
units.en: Yang Shihou came from Jingou in Ying prefecture.
units.literal: Yang Shihou was a native of Jingou in Ying prefecture.

units.zh: 少事河陽李罕之，罕之降晉，選其麾下勁卒百人獻於晉王，師厚在籍中。
units.en: As a youth he served Li Hanzhi of Heyang. When Hanzhi went over to Jin, he picked a hundred of his best men and sent them to the Prince of Jin; Shihou was one of them.
units.literal: In youth he served Li Hanzhi of Heyang; when Hanzhi surrendered to Jin, he selected a hundred stalwart soldiers from his command and presented them to the Prince of Jin; Shihou was among them.

units.zh: 師厚在晉，無所知名，後以罪奔於梁，太祖以為宣武軍押衙、曹州刺史。
units.en: Shihou made no name in Jin. Later he fled to Liang for a crime, and Taizu of Liang made him yabing of the Xuanwu army and prefect of Cao.
units.literal: Shihou won no fame in Jin service; later he fled to Liang on account of a crime, and Taizu of Liang made him yabing of the Xuanwu army and prefect of Cao.

units.zh: 梁攻王師範，師厚戰臨朐，擒其偏將八十餘人，取棣州，以功拜齊州刺史。
units.en: When Liang attacked Wang Shifan, Shihou fought at Linqu, took more than eighty of Shifan’s officers, seized Di prefecture, and was rewarded with Qi prefecture.
units.literal: When Liang attacked Wang Shifan, Shihou fought at Linqu, captured more than eighty of Shifan’s junior generals, took Di prefecture, and was made prefect of Qi for his merit.

units.zh: 太祖攻趙匡凝於襄陽，遣師厚為先鋒。
units.en: Taizu of Liang struck Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang and put Shihou in the van.
units.literal: Taizu of Liang attacked Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang and sent Shihou as vanguard.

units.zh: 師厚取谷城西童山木為浮橋，渡漢水，擊匡凝，敗之，匡凝棄城走。
units.en: Shihou felled timber on Tong Mountain west of the valley city, bridged the Han, smashed Kuangning, and drove him from the city.
units.literal: Shihou took timber from Tong Mountain west of the valley city to build a pontoon bridge, crossed the Han River, struck Kuangning, defeated him, and Kuangning abandoned the city and fled.

units.zh: 師厚進攻荊南，又走匡凝弟匡明，功為多，拜山南東道節度使、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: Shihou pushed into Jingnan and routed Kuangning’s brother Kuangming; for that he was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit and co-equal grand councilor.
units.literal: Shihou pressed into Jingnan, routed Kuangning’s brother Kuangming as well, won great distinction, and was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit and co-equal grand councilor.

units.zh: 劉知俊叛，攻陷長安，劉掞、牛存節等攻之，久不克。
units.en: When Liu Zhijun rebelled and took Chang’an, Liu Yan and Niu Cunjie besieged him for months without success.
units.literal: Liu Zhijun rebelled and captured Chang’an; Liu Yan and Niu Cunjie besieged him but could not take the city for a long time.

units.zh: 師厚以奇兵出，旁南山入其西門，降其守者，遂克之。
units.en: Shihou slipped a surprise force along the southern hills into the west gate, won over the defenders, and took the city.
units.literal: Shihou led surprise troops out, entered by the west gate along the southern mountains, and persuaded the garrison to surrender; the city was then taken.

units.zh: 晉周德威攻晉州以應知俊，師厚敗之於蒙坑，以功遷保義軍節度使，徙鎮宣義。
units.en: When Zhou Dewei of Jin struck Jin prefecture to aid Zhijun, Shihou crushed him at Mengkeng and, for his merit, was appointed military governor of Baoyi and then transferred to Xuanyi.
units.literal: Zhou Dewei of Jin attacked Jin prefecture in support of Zhijun; Shihou defeated him at Mengkeng and, for his merit, was transferred to military governor of Baoyi and moved to govern Xuanyi.

units.zh: 是時，梁兵攻趙久無功，太祖病臥洛陽，少間，乃自將北擊趙。
units.en: Liang had besieged Zhao for months without result. Taizu lay sick at Luoyang; when he rallied slightly he marched north in person against Zhao.
units.literal: At that time Liang troops had besieged Zhao for a long time without success; Taizu lay ill at Luoyang; after a slight recovery he personally led a northern campaign against Zhao.

units.zh: 師厚從太祖至洹水，夜行迷失道，明旦，次魏縣，聞敵將至，梁兵潰亂不可止，久之無敵，乃定。
units.en: Shihou followed Taizu to Huanshui. A night march went wrong; at dawn they halted at Wei county. Word came that enemy commanders were near, and the Liang host dissolved in panic—only after a long wait, with no foe in sight, did they steady.
units.literal: Shihou followed Taizu to Huanshui; they marched at night and lost their way; at dawn they halted at Wei county; hearing that enemy commanders were approaching, the Liang army broke in chaos beyond control; after a long while with no enemy appearing, order returned.

units.zh: 已而太祖疾作，乃還。
units.en: Soon Taizu’s sickness returned and he turned back.
units.literal: Before long Taizu’s illness flared again and he withdrew.

units.zh: 明年少間，而晉軍攻燕，燕王劉守光求援於梁，太祖為之擊趙以牽晉，屯於龍花，遣師厚攻棗強，三月不能下。
units.en: The next year, barely recovered, he learned that Jin was attacking Yan and that Prince Liu Shouguang had begged Liang for help. Taizu hit Zhao to pin Jin, camped at Longhua, and sent Shihou against Zaoqiang—which held out three months.
units.literal: The next year, after a slight recovery, Jin forces attacked Yan; Liu Shouguang the Prince of Yan sought Liang’s aid; Taizu struck Zhao to tie down Jin, encamped at Longhua, and sent Shihou against Zaoqiang, which after three months still would not fall.

units.zh: 太祖怒，自往督兵戰，乃破，屠之，進圍蓚縣。
units.en: Taizu came in fury to direct the assault himself. The city fell and was put to the sword; the army then moved to besiege Zhuo county.
units.literal: Taizu in anger went in person to oversee the assault until it broke; they slaughtered the population and advanced to besiege Zhuo county.

units.zh: 晉史建瑭以輕兵夜擊梁軍，梁軍大擾，太祖與師厚皆棄輜重南走。
units.en: Shi Jiantang of Jin hit the Liang camp at night with light troops. The army broke in uproar; Taizu and Shihou cast off their baggage and fled south.
units.literal: Shi Jiantang of Jin led light troops in a night strike on the Liang camp; the Liang army was thrown into great disorder; Taizu and Shihou both abandoned their baggage trains and fled south.

units.zh: 太祖還東都，師厚留屯魏州。
units.en: Taizu went back to the eastern capital; Shihou stayed at Weizhou.
units.literal: Taizu returned to the eastern capital; Shihou remained encamped at Weizhou.

units.zh: 明年，太祖遇弒，友珪自立，師厚乘間殺魏牙將潘晏、臧延範等，逐出節度使羅周翰，友珪因以師厚為天雄軍節度使。
units.en: The next year Taizu was murdered and Yougui seized the throne. Shihou took the chance to kill the Wei garrison officers Pan Yan and Zang Yanfan, drive out the military governor Luo Zhouhan, and Yougui made him military governor of Tianxiong.
units.literal: The next year Taizu was assassinated; Yougui seized power; Shihou seized the moment to kill the Wei garrison officers Pan Yan, Zang Yanfan, and others, expelled the military governor Luo Zhouhan, and Yougui installed Shihou as military governor of Tianxiong.

units.zh: 自太祖與晉戰河北，師厚常為招討使，悉領梁之勁兵。
units.en: Ever since Taizu’s wars with Jin in Hebei, Shihou had served as pacification commissioner and commanded Liang’s finest troops.
units.literal: From the time Taizu fought Jin in Hebei, Shihou had regularly served as pacification commissioner and held all of Liang’s best troops.

units.zh: 太祖崩，師厚遂逐其帥，而稍矜倨難制。
units.en: After Taizu died Shihou expelled his own commander and grew proud and hard to manage.
units.literal: After Taizu’s death Shihou drove out his own commander and grew somewhat proud and difficult to control.

units.zh: 時魏恃牙兵，其帥得以倔強。
units.en: Wei then lived by its garrison troops, and its commanders could afford to be stubborn.
units.literal: At that time Wei relied on its garrison troops, enabling its commanders to defy authority.

units.zh: 羅紹威時，牙兵盡死，魏勢孤，始為梁所制。
units.en: Under Luo Shaowei the garrison troops were destroyed; Wei stood alone and at last fell fully under Liang’s hand.
units.literal: Under Luo Shaowei the garrison troops were wiped out; Wei stood alone and only then came fully under Liang’s control.

units.zh: 師厚已得志，乃復置銀槍效範軍。
units.en: Once Shihou had his way, he restored the Silver Lance Model Army.
units.literal: Once Shihou had his way, he re-established the Silver Lance Model Army.

units.zh: 友珪陰欲圖之，召師厚入計事。
units.en: Yougui secretly meant to destroy him and summoned Shihou to discuss state business.
units.literal: Yougui secretly plotted against him and summoned Shihou to consult on affairs.

units.zh: 其吏田溫等勸師厚勿行，師厚曰：「吾二十年不負朱家，今若不行，則見疑而生事，然吾知上為人，雖往，無如我何也。」
units.en: His clerk Tian Wen and others begged him not to go. Shihou said: “For twenty years I have never failed the Zhu house. If I stay away now, suspicion will breed trouble. Still, I know the man on the throne—even if I go, he cannot touch me.”
units.literal: His clerks Tian Wen and others urged Shihou not to go; Shihou said: “For twenty years I have never failed the Zhu family. If I do not go now, suspicion will arise and trouble follow. Yet I know what our lord is like—even if I go, he can do nothing to me.”

units.zh: 乃以勁兵二萬朝京師，留其兵城外，以十餘人自從，入見友珪，友珪益恐懼，賜與巨萬而還。
units.en: He marched twenty thousand crack troops to the capital, left them outside the walls, and entered with a dozen men. Yougui only grew more afraid, showered him with gifts, and let him go.
units.literal: Then he led twenty thousand crack troops to court, left them outside the city walls, and entered with only a dozen or so followers to see Yougui; Yougui grew only more fearful, lavished vast gifts on him, and sent him back.

units.zh: 已而末帝謀討友珪，問於趙巖，巖曰：「此事成敗，在招討楊公爾。
units.en: Later the Last Emperor plotted against Yougui and asked Zhao Yan. Yan said: “Whether this succeeds or fails rests on Pacification Commissioner Yang.
units.literal: Later the Last Emperor plotted to overthrow Yougui and consulted Zhao Yan; Yan said: “Success or failure in this matter rests on Pacification Commissioner Yang alone.

units.zh: 得其一言諭禁軍，吾事立辦。」
units.en: One word to the palace guard from him, and our work is finished.”
units.literal: One word from him to the palace guard, and our business is done.”

units.zh: 末帝乃遣馬慎交陰見師厚，布腹心。
units.en: The Last Emperor sent Ma Shenjiao to Shihou in secret and opened his heart to him.
units.literal: The Last Emperor then sent Ma Shenjiao secretly to see Shihou and lay bare his heart.

units.zh: 師厚猶豫未決，謂其下曰：「方郢王弒逆時，吾不能即討。
units.en: Shihou wavered. He told his officers: “When Prince E committed regicide, I could not move at once.
units.literal: Shihou hesitated and had not decided; he told his men: “When Prince E murdered his sovereign, I could not strike at once.

units.zh: 今君臣之分已定，無故改圖，人謂我何？」
units.en: Now the bond between lord and subject is fixed. To turn without cause—what will men say of me?”
units.literal: Now the bond between ruler and subject is settled. To change course without cause—what will men say of me?”

units.zh: 其下或曰：「友珪弒父與君，乃天下之惡，均王仗大義以誅賊，其事易成。
units.en: Some of his men said: “Yougui killed his father and lord—the worst villain alive. Prince Jun marches under righteous cause to destroy him; the deed is easily done.
units.literal: Some of his men said: “Yougui murdered his father and lord—the worst villain under heaven. Prince Jun wields righteous cause to destroy the criminal; the thing is easily done.

units.zh: 彼若一朝破賊，公將何以自處？」
units.en: If he breaks the villain in one morning, where will you stand then?”
units.literal: If he breaks the villain in a single morning, where will you stand?”

units.zh: 師厚大悟，乃遣其將王舜賢至洛陽，見袁象先計事，使朱漢賓以兵屯滑州為應。
units.en: Shihou saw the truth of it. He sent Wang Shunxian to Luoyang to plan with Yuan Xiangxian and posted Zhu Hanbin at Huazhou in support.
units.literal: Shihou saw the point; he sent his officer Wang Shunxian to Luoyang to consult Yuan Xiangxian and posted Zhu Hanbin’s troops at Huazhou in support.

units.zh: 末帝卒與象先殺友珪。
units.en: The Last Emperor and Xiangxian at last killed Yougui.
units.literal: The Last Emperor at last joined Xiangxian in killing Yougui.

units.zh: 末帝即位，封師厚鄴王，詔書不名，事無巨細皆以諮之，然心益忌而畏之。
units.en: When the Last Emperor took the throne he enfeoffed Shihou as Prince of Ye. Edicts did not name him; affairs great and small were all referred to him, yet the emperor grew ever more jealous and afraid of him.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne he enfeoffed Shihou as Prince of Ye; edicts did not name him; affairs great and small were all referred to him, yet the emperor grew ever more jealous and fearful of him.

units.zh: 已而師厚瘍發卒，末帝為之受賀於宮中。
units.en: Before long Shihou died of carbuncle, and the Last Emperor received congratulations for it within the palace.
units.literal: Before long Shihou died of carbuncle, and the Last Emperor received congratulations for it within the palace.

units.zh: 由是始分相、魏為兩鎮。
units.en: From this Xiang and Wei were first divided into two commands.
units.literal: From this the division of Xiang and Wei into two commands began.

units.zh: 魏軍亂，以魏博降晉，梁失河北自此始。
units.en: Wei troops mutinied; Weibo went over to Jin, and Liang’s loss of Hebei began from this.
units.literal: Wei troops mutinied; Weibo surrendered to Jin, and Liang’s loss of Hebei began from this.

units.zh: 王景仁，廬州合淝人也。
units.en: Wang Jingren came from Hefei in Luzhou.
units.literal: Wang Jingren was a native of Hefei in Luzhou.

units.zh: 初名茂章，少從楊行密起淮南。
units.en: He was first called Maozhang. As a youth he followed Yang Xingmi’s rise in Huainan.
units.literal: Originally named Maozhang; in youth he followed Yang Xingmi’s rise in Huainan.

units.zh: 景仁為將驍勇剛悍，質略無威儀，臨敵務以身先士卒，行密壯之。
units.en: Jingren fought with fierce, blunt courage and no show of rank; in battle he always led from the front. Xingmi admired him.
units.literal: As a commander Jingren was fierce and daring, plain and without imposing bearing; in battle he always led from the front; Xingmi admired him.

units.zh: 梁太祖遣子友寧攻王師範於青州，師範乞兵於行密，行密遣景仁以步騎七千救師範。
units.en: Taizu of Liang sent his son Youning against Wang Shifan at Qingzhou. Shifan begged Xingmi for aid, and Xingmi sent Jingren with seven thousand foot and horse to relieve him.
units.literal: Taizu of Liang sent his son Youning against Wang Shifan at Qingzhou; Shifan begged troops from Xingmi, who sent Jingren with seven thousand foot and horse to rescue Shifan.

units.zh: 師範以兵背城為兩柵，友寧夜擊其一柵，柵中告急，趣景仁出戰，景仁按兵不動。
units.en: Shifan built two palisaded camps with his back to the wall. Youning struck one by night; the camp cried for help and begged Jingren out, but Jingren held his men still.
units.literal: Shifan built two palisaded camps with his back to the city wall; Youning attacked one camp by night; the camp cried for help and urged Jingren out, but Jingren held his troops still.

units.zh: 友寧已破一柵，連戰不已。
units.en: Youning broke one camp and kept fighting without rest.
units.literal: Youning broke one camp and continued fighting without pause.

units.zh: 遲明，景仁度友寧兵已困，乃出戰，大敗之，遂斬友寧，以其首報行密。
units.en: At dawn Jingren judged Youning’s men spent, went out, and routed them. He beheaded Youning and sent the head to Xingmi.
units.literal: At dawn Jingren judged Youning’s men spent, went out, routed them utterly, beheaded Youning, and sent the head to Xingmi.

units.zh: 是時，梁太祖方攻鄆州，聞子友寧死，以兵二十萬倍道而至，景仁閉壘示怯，伺梁兵怠，毀柵而出，驅馳疾戰，戰酣退坐，召諸將飲酒，已而復戰。
units.en: Taizu was then besieging Yun prefecture. When he heard of Youning’s death he came with two hundred thousand men at forced march. Jingren shut the ramparts and played timid; when Liang slackened he tore down the palisades and charged. Battle ran hot; he withdrew to sit, called his generals to drink, then went back in.
units.literal: At that time Taizu was investing Yun prefecture; hearing of Youning’s death he came with two hundred thousand men at forced march; Jingren shut the ramparts and feigned timidity; when Liang troops slackened he tore down the palisades and charged in wild battle—fighting fiercely, he withdrew to sit, summoned the generals to drink, then returned to the fight.

units.zh: 太祖登高望見之，得青州降人，問：「飲酒者為誰？」
units.en: Taizu watched from a height and questioned a Qingzhou defector: “Who is the man drinking?”
units.literal: Taizu watched from a height and got a Qingzhou defector; he asked: “Who is the one drinking?”

units.zh: 曰：「王茂章也。」
units.en: “Maozhang,” he said.
units.literal: He said: “Maozhang.”

units.zh: 太祖嘆曰：「使吾得此人為將，天下不足平也！」
units.en: Taizu sighed: “Had I such a man for a general, all under heaven would not be hard to pacify!”
units.literal: Taizu sighed and said: “Could I have this man as my general, all under heaven would not be hard to pacify!”

units.zh: 梁兵又敗。
units.en: Liang was beaten again.
units.literal: Liang troops were beaten again.

units.zh: 景仁軍還，梁兵急追之，景仁度不可走，遣裨將李虔裕以眾一旅設覆於山下以待之，留軍不行，解鞍而寢。
units.en: Jingren’s army withdrew; Liang pressed hard. Seeing he could not outrun them, Jingren sent Li Qianyu with one brigade to lie in ambush below the hills, kept the main force still, unbridled his horse, and slept.
units.literal: Jingren’s army retreated; Liang gave hot pursuit; Jingren saw flight impossible, sent the junior commander Li Qianyu with one brigade to lay an ambush in the hills below to await them, kept the main force still, unbridled his horse and slept.

units.zh: 虔裕疾呼曰：「追兵至矣，宜速走，虔裕以死遏之！」
units.en: Qianyu cried out: “Pursuers are here—you must flee now; Qianyu will hold them with his life!”
units.literal: Qianyu shouted urgently: “Pursuers are upon us—you must flee at once; Qianyu will hold them with his life!”

units.zh: 景仁曰：「吾亦戰於此也。」
units.en: Jingren said: “I will fight here too.”
units.literal: Jingren said: “I too will fight here.”

units.zh: 虔裕三請，景仁乃行，而虔裕卒戰死，梁兵以故不能及，而景仁全軍以歸。
units.en: Qianyu begged three times; Jingren only then rode off. Qianyu died fighting; Liang could not catch up, and Jingren brought the whole army home.
units.literal: Qianyu pleaded three times; Jingren only then departed; Qianyu died fighting; Liang could not catch up, and Jingren brought the whole army home safely.

units.zh: 景仁事行密，為潤州團練使。
units.en: Under Xingmi he was made regimental commander of Runzhou.
units.literal: Serving Xingmi, Jingren was made regimental commander of Runzhou.

units.zh: 行密死，子渥自宣州入立，以景仁代守宣州。
units.en: When Xingmi died his son Wo came from Xuanzhou to take power and left Jingren to hold Xuanzhou.
units.literal: After Xingmi died his son Wo came from Xuanzhou to take the throne and set Jingren to hold Xuanzhou in his stead.

units.zh: 渥已立，反求宣州故物，景仁惜不與，渥怒，以兵攻之。
units.en: Once enthroned, Wo demanded Xuanzhou’s old stores back. Jingren would not yield; Wo raged and attacked.
units.literal: Once enthroned Wo demanded back the old possessions of Xuanzhou; Jingren grudged giving them; Wo raged and attacked.

units.zh: 景仁奔於錢镠，镠表景仁領宣州節度使。
units.en: Jingren fled to Qian Liu, who memorialized to make him military governor of Xuanzhou.
units.literal: Jingren fled to Qian Liu; Liu memorialized Jingren as military governor of Xuanzhou.

units.zh: 梁太祖素識景仁，乃遣人召之，景仁間道歸梁，仍以為寧國軍節度使，加同中書門下平章事。
units.en: Taizu had long known Jingren and sent for him. Jingren came to Liang by hidden routes and was made military governor of Ningguo and co-equal grand councilor.
units.literal: Taizu had long known Jingren; he sent men to summon him; Jingren came to Liang by secret paths and was made military governor of Ningguo and co-equal grand councilor.

units.zh: 久之，未有以用，使參宰相班，奉朝請而已。
units.en: For a long while he had no real post—he sat among the chancellors as a court attendant only.
units.literal: For a long while he had no real assignment—he sat in the chancellor’s ranks as a court attendant only.

units.zh: 開平四年，以景仁為北面招討使，將韓勍、李思安等兵伐趙，行至魏州，司天監言：「太陰虧，不利行師。」
units.en: In the fourth year of Kaiping Jingren was made northern-route pacification commissioner and led Han Qing, Li Si’an, and others against Zhao. At Weizhou the Directorate of Astronomy said: “The moon is in eclipse—unfavorable for taking the field.”
units.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiping Jingren was made northern-route pacification commissioner and led Han Qing, Li Si’an, and other troops against Zhao. When they reached Weizhou the Directorate of Astronomy said: “The moon is in eclipse—unfavorable for taking the field.”

units.zh: 太祖亟召景仁等還，已而復遣之。
units.en: Taizu urgently recalled Jingren and the others, then sent them out again.
units.literal: Taizu urgently recalled Jingren and the others, then sent them out again.

units.zh: 景仁已去，太祖思術者言，馳使者止景仁於魏以待。
units.en: Jingren had already left when Taizu, remembering the diviner’s warning, sent a messenger at speed to halt him at Wei and await further orders.
units.literal: Jingren had already departed when Taizu, remembering the diviner’s words, dispatched a messenger at speed to halt him at Wei to await orders.

units.zh: 景仁已過邢、洺，使者及之，景仁不奉詔，進營於柏鄉。
units.en: Jingren had already passed Xing and Ming when the messenger caught up; Jingren refused the edict and advanced to camp at Baixiang.
units.literal: Jingren had already passed Xing and Ming when the messenger reached him; Jingren did not obey the edict and advanced to encamp at Baixiang.

units.zh: 乾化元年正月庚寅，日有食之，崇政使敬翔白太祖曰：「兵可憂矣！」
units.en: On gengyin, the first month of Qianhua 1, there was a solar eclipse. Jing Xiang, commissioner of the Chongzheng Bureau, told Taizu: “The army ought to worry!”
units.literal: On gengyin, the first month of the first year of Qianhua, there was a solar eclipse. Jing Xiang, commissioner of the Chongzheng Bureau, told Taizu: “The army ought to worry!”

units.zh: 太祖為之旰食。
units.en: Taizu went without his noon meal on account of it.
units.literal: Taizu went without his noon meal on account of it.

units.zh: 是日，景仁及晉人戰，大敗於柏鄉，景仁歸訴於太祖，太祖曰：「吾亦知之，蓋韓勍、李思安輕汝為客，不從節度爾。」
units.en: That day Jingren fought the Jin and was routed at Baixiang. Jingren returned and complained to Taizu. Taizu said: “I know it too—Han Qing and Li Si’an look down on you as an outsider and would not obey your command.”
units.literal: That day Jingren fought the Jin forces and was badly defeated at Baixiang. Jingren returned and complained to Taizu; Taizu said: “I know it too—Han Qing and Li Si’an look down on you as an outsider and would not obey your command.”

units.zh: 乃罷景仁就第，後數月，悉復其官爵。
units.en: Jingren was dismissed and sent home; several months later all his offices and titles were fully restored.
units.literal: Jingren was dismissed and sent to his private residence; several months later all his offices and titles were fully restored.

units.zh: 末帝立，以景仁為淮南招討使，攻廬、壽，軍過獨山，山有楊行密祠，景仁再拜號泣而去。
units.en: When the Last Emperor took the throne Jingren was made Huainan pacification commissioner and attacked Lu and Shou. At Dushan, where Yang Xingmi had a shrine, he bowed twice, wept aloud, and went on.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne Jingren was made pacification commissioner for Huainan and attacked Lu and Shou; passing Dushan with its shrine to Yang Xingmi he bowed twice, wailed, and went on.

units.zh: 戰於霍山，梁兵敗走，景仁殿而力戰，以故梁兵不甚敗。
units.en: At Huo Mountain Liang was routed. Jingren covered the retreat and fought with all his strength, so the defeat was not utter ruin.
units.literal: At Huo Mountain Liang was routed; Jingren covered the retreat and fought with all his strength, so Liang’s defeat was not total catastrophe.

units.zh: 景仁歸京師，病疽卒，贈太尉。
units.en: Jingren returned to the capital, died of carbuncle, and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
units.literal: Jingren returned to the capital, died of carbuncle, and was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 賀瓌，字光遠，濮州人也。
units.en: He Gui, courtesy name Guangyuan, came from Pu prefecture.
units.literal: He Gui, courtesy name Guangyuan, was a native of Pu prefecture.

units.zh: 事鄆州朱宣為都指揮使。
units.en: He served Zhu Xuan of Yun prefecture as overall commander.
units.literal: He served Zhu Xuan of Yun prefecture as overall commander.

units.zh: 梁太祖攻朱瑾於兗州，宣遣瑰與何懷寶、柳存等以兵萬人救兗州，瑰趨待賓館，欲絕梁餉道。
units.en: Taizu of Liang attacked Zhu Jin at Yan prefecture. Xuan sent Gui with He Huaibao, Liu Cun, and others—ten thousand men—to relieve Yan. Gui raced for the Guest Reception Hall to cut Liang’s supply line.
units.literal: Taizu of Liang attacked Zhu Jin at Yan prefecture; Xuan sent Gui with He Huaibao, Liu Cun, and others with ten thousand men to relieve Yan; Gui hurried to the Guest Reception Hall intending to cut Liang’s supply line.

units.zh: 梁太祖略地至中都，得降卒，言瑰等兵趨待賓館矣！
units.en: Taizu overran the country to Zhongdu and took a defector who said Gui’s army was racing for the Guest Reception Hall.
units.literal: Taizu overran the land to Zhongdu and got a defector who said Gui’s force was heading for the Guest Reception Hall!

units.zh: 以六壬占之，得「斬關」，以為吉，乃選精兵夜疾馳百里，期先至待賓以逆瑰，而夜黑，兵失道，旦至鉅野東，遇瑰兵，擊之，瑰等大敗。
units.en: He cast the liu-ren oracle and drew “Cut the Pass”—a good sign. He picked elite troops and raced a hundred li by night to reach the Guest Reception Hall before Gui. In the dark the army lost the road; at dawn east of Juye they met Gui, struck, and routed him.
units.literal: He cast liu-ren divination and got “Cut the Pass,” deeming it auspicious; he selected elite troops and raced a hundred li by night, intending to reach the Guest Reception Hall before Gui; in darkness the army lost the road; at dawn east of Juye they met Gui’s force, struck, and Gui suffered great defeat.

units.zh: 瑰走，梁兵急追之，瑰顧路窮，登冢上大呼曰：「我賀瑰也，可勿殺我！」
units.en: Gui fled; Liang pressed hard. Seeing the road at an end, Gui climbed a tomb mound and shouted: “I am He Gui—do not kill me!”
units.literal: Gui fled; Liang pressed hard; seeing the road exhausted Gui climbed a tomb mound and cried: “I am He Gui—do not kill me!”

units.zh: 太祖馳騎取之，並取懷寶等數十人，降其卒三千餘人。
units.en: Taizu galloped up and took him, along with Huaibao and several dozen others, and accepted the surrender of more than three thousand men.
units.literal: Taizu spurred his horse to take him; he also captured Huaibao and several dozen others and accepted the surrender of more than three thousand soldiers.

units.zh: 是日，大風揚沙蔽天，太祖曰：「天怒我殺人少邪？」
units.en: That day a great wind raised sand and hid the sky. Taizu said: “Does heaven rage that I kill too few?”
units.literal: That day a great wind raised sand and veiled the sky; Taizu said: “Does heaven rage that I kill too few?”

units.zh: 即盡殺降卒三千人，而系瑰及懷寶等至兗城下以招瑾，瑾不納，因斬懷寶等十餘人，而獨留瑰。
units.en: He then slaughtered all three thousand captives, bound Gui and Huaibao and the rest below Yan city to summon Jin, but Jin would not take them in. He beheaded Huaibao and more than ten others and kept Gui alone.
units.literal: He then slaughtered all three thousand surrendered soldiers, bound Gui and Huaibao and the rest below Yan city to summon Jin, but Jin would not accept them; he therefore beheaded Huaibao and more than ten others but kept Gui alone.

units.zh: 瑰感太祖不殺，誓以身自效。
units.en: Moved that Taizu had spared him, Gui vowed to give his life in service.
units.literal: Gui was moved that Taizu spared him and vowed to devote his body in service.

units.zh: 從太祖平青州，以為曹州刺史。
units.en: When Taizu pacified Qing prefecture, Gui was made prefect of Cao.
units.literal: Following Taizu in pacifying Qing prefecture he was made prefect of Cao.

units.zh: 太祖即位，累遷相州刺史。
units.en: When Taizu took the throne he rose step by step to prefect of Xiang.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne he was promoted in stages to prefect of Xiang.

units.zh: 末帝時，遷左龍虎統軍，宣義軍節度使。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor he became left Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief and military governor of Xuanyi.
units.literal: Under the Last Emperor he was made left Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief and military governor of Xuanyi.

units.zh: 貞明元年，魏兵亂，賀德倫降晉，晉王入魏州。
units.en: In the first year of Zhenming Wei troops mutinied. He Delun went over to Jin, and the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhenming Wei troops mutinied; He Delun surrendered to Jin, and the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou.

units.zh: 劉鄩敗于故元城，走黎陽，貝、衞、洺、磁諸州皆入于晉。
units.en: Liu Xun was beaten at former Yuancheng and fled to Liyang. Bei, Wei, Ming, and Ci prefectures all passed to Jin.
units.literal: Liu Xun was defeated at former Yuancheng and fled to Liyang; Bei, Wei, Ming, and Ci prefectures all passed to Jin.

units.zh: 晉軍取楊劉，末帝乃以瓌為招討使，與謝彥章等屯于行臺。
units.en: Jin took Yangliu. The Last Emperor then made Gui pacification commissioner and camped with Xie Yanzhang and others at the field headquarters.
units.literal: Jin troops took Yangliu; the Last Emperor then made Gui pacification commissioner and encamped with Xie Yanzhang and others at the field headquarters.

units.zh: 晉軍迫瓌十里而柵，相持百餘日。
units.en: Jin pressed within ten li of Gui and fenced in; the standoff lasted more than a hundred days.
units.literal: Jin troops pressed within ten li of Gui and palisaded; the stalemate lasted more than a hundred days.

units.zh: 瓌與彥章有隙，伏甲殺之，莊宗喜曰：「將帥不和，梁亡無日矣！」
units.en: Gui and Yanzhang were at odds. Gui hid armed men and killed him. Zhuangzong rejoiced and said: “When commanders fall out, Liang’s end is near!”
units.literal: Gui and Yanzhang were at odds; he hid armored men and killed him. Zhuangzong rejoiced and said: “When commanders are not at one, Liang’s fall is near!”

units.zh: 乃令軍中歸其老疾於鄴，以輕兵襲濮州。
units.en: He then sent the old and sick back to Ye and struck Pu prefecture with light troops.
units.literal: He then ordered the army to send the old and sick back to Ye and struck Pu prefecture with light troops.

units.zh: 瓌自行臺躡之，戰于胡柳陂，晉人輜重在陣西，瓌軍將薄之，晉軍亂，斬其將周德威，盡取其輜重。
units.en: Gui pursued from the field headquarters himself and fought at Huliupi. Jin baggage trains lay west of the formation; as Gui’s army was about to close, the Jin broke in disorder. They beheaded Zhou Dewei and took all the baggage trains.
units.literal: Gui pursued from the field headquarters himself and fought at Huliupi. Jin baggage trains were west of the formation; Gui’s army was about to press them when the Jin forces broke in disorder. They beheaded the commander Zhou Dewei and took all the baggage trains.

units.zh: 軍已勝，陣無石山，日暮，晉兵仰攻之，瓌軍下山擊晉軍，瓌大敗，晉遂取濮州，城德勝，夾河為柵。
units.en: The army had already won, but there was no stony hill in the formation. At dusk the Jin attacked uphill; Gui’s army went down the hill to strike them and was routed. Jin then took Pu, fortified Desheng, and fenced both banks of the river.
units.literal: The army had already won; there was no stony hill in the formation. At dusk Jin troops attacked uphill; Gui’s army went down the hill to strike the Jin forces and Gui suffered great defeat. Jin then took Pu prefecture, fortified Desheng, and fenced both banks of the river.

units.zh: 瓌以舟兵攻南柵，不能得，還軍行臺，以疾卒，年六十二，贈侍中。
units.en: Gui attacked the southern palisade with river troops but could not take it. He returned to the field headquarters, died of illness at sixty-two, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
units.literal: Gui attacked the southern palisade with river troops but could not take it. He returned the army to the field headquarters, died of illness at sixty-two, and was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 有子光圖。
units.en: He had a son Guangtu.
units.literal: He had a son Guangtu.

units.zh: 凡言有子某者，皆仕皇朝有聞。
units.en: Wherever the text says a man had a son, that son later won renown in service to the imperial court.
units.literal: Wherever it says a man had a son, that son later won renown in service to the imperial court.

units.zh: 王檀，字眾美，京兆人也。
units.en: Wang Tan, courtesy name Zhongmei, came from Jingzhao.
units.literal: Wang Tan, courtesy name Zhongmei, was a native of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 少事梁太祖為小校，尚讓攻梁，戰尉氏門，檀勇出諸將，太祖奇之，遷踏白副指揮使。
units.en: As a youth he served Taizu of Liang as a minor officer. When Shang Rang attacked Liang at the Weishi Gate, Tan’s courage outshone the other commanders; Taizu noted him and made him deputy commander of the scout corps.
units.literal: In youth he served Taizu of Liang as a minor officer; when Shang Rang attacked Liang at the Weishi Gate Tan’s bravery exceeded the other commanders; Taizu marked him and made him deputy commander of the Footwhite corps.

units.zh: 從朱珍募兵東方，戰數有功。
units.en: He followed Zhu Zhen east to raise troops and won merit in battle after battle.
units.literal: He followed Zhu Zhen in recruiting troops in the east and won merit in repeated battles.

units.zh: 梁與蔡兵戰板橋，李重裔馬踣，為蔡兵所擒，檀馳取之，並獲其將一人。
units.en: Liang and Cai fought at Banqiao. Li Chongyi’s horse stumbled and Cai took him; Tan galloped in, recovered him, and captured one of their commanders.
units.literal: Liang and Cai troops fought at Banqiao; Li Chongyi’s horse stumbled and Cai captured him; Tan galloped and recovered him, also taking one of their commanders.

units.zh: 從太祖破魏內黃，遷沖山都虞候。
units.en: When Taizu broke Neihuang in Wei, Tan was made chief adjutant of Chong Mountain.
units.literal: Following Taizu in breaking Neihuang in Wei he was promoted to chief adjutant of Chong Mountain.

units.zh: 復從朱珍攻徐州，檀獲其將一人。
units.en: Again with Zhu Zhen against Xu prefecture he captured one of their commanders.
units.literal: Again following Zhu Zhen against Xu prefecture Tan captured one of their commanders.

units.zh: 梁兵攻王師範，檀以一軍破其密州，拜密州刺史。
units.en: When Liang attacked Wang Shifan, Tan with one army broke Mi prefecture and was made its prefect.
units.literal: When Liang attacked Wang Shifan Tan with one army broke his Mi prefecture and was made prefect of Mi.

units.zh: 太祖即位，遷保義軍節度使，潞州東北面招討使。
units.en: When Taizu took the throne Tan was made military governor of Baoyi and pacification commissioner for the northeast of Lu.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne Tan was made military governor of Baoyi and pacification commissioner for the northeast of Lu prefecture.

units.zh: 王景仁敗於柏鄉，晉兵圍邢州，太祖大懼，欲自將救之，檀止太祖，請自拒敵，力戰，卒全邢州，以功加同中書門下平章事，進封瑯琊郡王。
units.en: When Wang Jingren lost at Baixiang and Jin besieged Xing prefecture, Taizu was deeply afraid and meant to rescue it in person. Tan stopped him, asked to hold the enemy himself, fought with all his strength, and at last saved Xing. For that he was made co-equal grand councilor and advanced to Prince of Langya.
units.literal: Wang Jingren lost at Baixiang; Jin troops besieged Xing prefecture; Taizu was greatly afraid and meant to lead the rescue himself; Tan stopped Taizu, asked to hold the enemy himself, fought with all strength, at last preserved Xing prefecture, was made co-equal grand councilor, and advanced to Prince of Langya commandery.

units.zh: 友珪立，徙鎮宣化。
units.en: When Yougui took the throne Tan was moved to Xuanhua.
units.literal: When Yougui took the throne Tan was moved to govern Xuanhua.

units.zh: 貞明元年又徙匡國。
units.en: In the first year of Zhenming he was moved again to Kuangguo.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he was again moved to Kuangguo.

units.zh: 是時，莊宗取魏博，檀以謂晉兵悉在河北，乃以奇兵西出陰地襲太原，不克而還。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Weibo, Tan judged that all Jin troops were in Hebei and led a surprise force west through Yin territory to raid Taiyuan. They did not take it and returned.
units.literal: At that time Zhuangzong took Weibo; Tan judged that all Jin troops were in Hebei and led surprise forces west through Yin territory to raid Taiyuan; they did not take it and returned.

units.zh: 徙鎮天平，檀嘗招納亡盜居帳下，帳下兵亂，入殺檀，年五十八，贈太師，謚曰忠毅。
units.en: Moved to Tianping, Tan had often taken in outlaws and fugitives under his tent. His tent troops mutinied, entered, and killed him. He was fifty-eight. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute.
units.literal: Moved to govern Tianping Tan had often recruited outlaws and fugitives under his tent; his tent troops mutinied, entered and killed Tan; he was fifty-eight; he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute.

units.zh: 馬嗣勳，濠州鍾離人也，少事州為客將，為人材武有辯。
units.en: Ma Sixun came from Zhongli in Haozhou. As a youth he served the prefecture as a guest general; he was talented in arms and eloquent.
units.literal: Ma Sixun was a native of Zhongli in Haozhou. In youth he served the prefecture as a guest general; he was talented in arms and eloquent.

units.zh: 梁太祖攻濠州，刺史張遂遣嗣勳持牌印降梁。
units.en: When Taizu of Liang attacked Haozhou, prefect Zhang Sui sent Sixun with the seal and credentials to surrender to Liang.
units.literal: When Taizu of Liang attacked Haozhou, the prefect Zhang Sui sent Sixun with the seal and credentials to surrender to Liang.

units.zh: 楊行密攻遂，遂又使嗣勳乞兵於太祖。
units.en: Yang Xingmi attacked Sui, and Sui again sent Sixun to beg troops from Taizu.
units.literal: Yang Xingmi attacked Sui; Sui again sent Sixun to beg troops from Taizu.

units.zh: 梁兵未至，濠州已沒，嗣勳無所歸，乃留事梁，太祖以為宣武軍元從押衙。
units.en: Liang troops had not arrived when Haozhou fell. Sixun had nowhere to go and stayed to serve Liang; Taizu made him yabing, an original follower of the Xuanwu army.
units.literal: Liang troops had not arrived when Haozhou fell; Sixun had nowhere to go and stayed to serve Liang; Taizu made him yabing, an original follower of the Xuanwu army.

units.zh: 太祖西攻鳳翔，行至華州，遣嗣勳入說韓建，建即時出降。
units.en: Taizu attacked Fengxiang in the west. Reaching Huazhou, he sent Sixun in to persuade Han Jian, who surrendered at once.
units.literal: Taizu attacked Fengxiang in the west; reaching Huazhou he sent Sixun in to persuade Han Jian, who surrendered at once.

units.zh: 天祐二年，羅紹威將誅牙軍，乞兵於梁，梁女嫁魏，適死，太祖乃遣嗣勳以長直千人為綵輿入魏，致兵器於輿中，聲言助葬。
units.en: In the second year of Tianyou Luo Shaowei meant to destroy the garrison troops and begged Liang for troops. A Liang princess married into Wei had just died; Taizu sent Sixun with a thousand Long-Direct troops in a funeral escort into Wei, weapons hidden in the carriage, claiming they came to assist the burial.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianyou Luo Shaowei meant to destroy the garrison troops and begged troops from Liang. A Liang princess married into Wei had just died; Taizu sent Sixun with a thousand Long-Direct troops as a funeral escort into Wei, weapons hidden in the carriage, proclaiming they came to assist the burial.

units.zh: 嗣勳館銅臺，夜與魏新鄉鎮兵攻石柱門，入迎紹威家屬，衞之。
units.en: Sixun lodged at the Bronze Terrace. By night he and the Xin township garrison troops of Wei attacked Shizhu Gate, entered to receive Shaowei’s household, and guarded them.
units.literal: Sixun lodged at the Bronze Terrace; by night he and the Xin township garrison troops of Wei attacked Shizhu Gate, entered to receive Shaowei’s household, and guarded them.

units.zh: 乃益取魏甲兵攻牙軍，牙軍不知兵所從來，莫能為備，殺其八千餘人，遲明皆盡。
units.en: He then took more of Wei’s armor and troops to attack the garrison troops. Not knowing where the soldiers had come from, they could not prepare; more than eight thousand were killed, and by dawn all were gone.
units.literal: He then took more of Wei’s armor and troops to attack the garrison troops. Not knowing where the soldiers had come from, they could not prepare; more than eight thousand were killed and by dawn all were gone.

units.zh: 嗣勳中重瘡卒。
units.en: Sixun was struck by grievous wounds and died.
units.literal: Sixun was struck by grievous wounds and died.

units.zh: 太祖即位，贈太保。
units.en: When Taizu took the throne Sixun was posthumously made Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne Sixun was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 王虔裕，瑯琊臨沂人也。
units.en: Wang Qianyu came from Linyi in Langya.
units.literal: Wang Qianyu was a native of Linyi in Langya.

units.zh: 為人健勇善騎射，以弋獵為生。
units.en: Hardy and brave, skilled in mounted archery, he made his living hunting with bow and net.
units.literal: As a man he was hardy and brave, skilled in mounted archery, and made his living by hunting with bow and net.

units.zh: 少從諸葛爽起青、棣間，其後爽為汝州防禦使，率兵北擊沙陀，還入長安攻黃巢。
units.en: As a youth he followed Zhuge Shuang’s rise between Qing and Di. Later, when Shuang was defense commissioner of Ru, he led troops north against the Shatuo and returned into Chang’an to attack Huang Chao.
units.literal: In youth he followed Zhuge Shuang’s rise between Qing and Di; later when Shuang was defense commissioner of Ru prefecture he led troops north against the Shatuo, returned into Chang’an to attack Huang Chao.

units.zh: 爽兵敗降巢，巢以爽為河陽節度使。
units.en: Shuang’s army was beaten and surrendered to Chao, who made him military governor of Heyang.
units.literal: Shuang’s army was defeated and surrendered to Chao; Chao made Shuang military governor of Heyang.

units.zh: 中和三年，孫儒陷河陽，虔裕隨爽奔於梁。
units.en: In the third year of Zhonghe Sun Ru took Heyang; Qianyu followed Shuang in flight to Liang.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhonghe Sun Ru took Heyang; Qianyu followed Shuang in flight to Liang.

units.zh: 是時，太祖新就鎮，黃巢、秦宗權等兵方盛，太祖數為所窘，而梁未有佗將，乃以虔裕將騎兵，常為先鋒擊巢陳、蔡間，拔其數柵。
units.en: Taizu had just taken command. Huang Chao, Qin Zongquan, and others were still strong; Taizu was often hard pressed and Liang had no other generals—so Qianyu was put in charge of cavalry, regularly leading the van against Chao between Chen and Cai and taking several palisades.
units.literal: At that time Taizu had newly taken command; Huang Chao, Qin Zongquan, and others’ armies were still strong; Taizu was often hard pressed and Liang had no other commanders—so Qianyu was put in charge of cavalry, regularly serving as vanguard in strikes against Chao between Chen and Cai, capturing several palisades.

units.zh: 巢走，梁兵躡之，戰於萬勝戍，賊敗而東，虔裕功為多，乃表虔裕義州刺史。
units.en: Chao fled; Liang pursued. At Wansheng post the bandits were routed eastward; Qianyu won the greatest merit, and Taizu memorialized to make him prefect of Yi.
units.literal: Chao fled; Liang troops pursued; they fought at Wansheng post; the bandits were routed eastward; Qianyu won greatest merit; Taizu memorialized to make Qianyu prefect of Yi.

units.zh: 黃巢已去，秦宗權攻許、鄭，與梁為敵境，大小百餘戰，虔裕常有功。
units.en: After Huang Chao was gone Qin Zongquan attacked Xu and Zheng. On the Liang border more than a hundred battles large and small were fought; Qianyu regularly distinguished himself.
units.literal: After Huang Chao was gone Qin Zongquan attacked Xu and Zheng; the border with Liang saw more than a hundred battles large and small; Qianyu regularly distinguished himself.

units.zh: 秦賢攻汴南境，太祖遣虔裕拒賢於尉氏，戰敗，失一裨將，太祖怒，拘虔裕於軍中。
units.en: Qin Xian struck Bian’s southern border. Taizu sent Qianyu to hold him at Weishi; they were beaten and lost a junior commander. Taizu raged and kept Qianyu under detention in the army.
units.literal: Qin Xian attacked the southern border of Bian; Taizu sent Qianyu to hold Xian at Weishi; they were defeated and lost one junior commander; Taizu raged and detained Qianyu in the army.

units.zh: 邢州孟遷降梁，為晉人所圍，太祖遣虔裕以精兵百人疾馳，夜破晉圍，入邢州，遲明，立梁旗幟於城上，晉人以為救兵至，乃退。
units.en: Meng Qian of Xing prefecture surrendered to Liang and was besieged by Jin. Taizu sent Qianyu with a hundred elite troops at forced march. By night they broke the Jin ring and entered Xing; at dawn they raised Liang banners on the walls. Jin thought relief had come and withdrew.
units.literal: Meng Qian of Xing prefecture surrendered to Liang and was besieged by Jin men; Taizu sent Qianyu with a hundred elite troops at forced march; by night they broke the Jin siege and entered Xing prefecture; at dawn they raised Liang banners on the walls; Jin men thought rescue had come and withdrew.

units.zh: 已而晉兵復來，遷執虔裕降於晉，見殺。
units.en: Before long the Jin returned; Meng Qian seized Qianyu and handed him over—they killed him.
units.literal: Before long Jin troops returned; Qian seized Qianyu and surrendered him to Jin; he was killed.

units.zh: 謝彥章
units.en: Xie Yanzhang
units.literal: Xie Yanzhang

units.zh: 謝彥章，許州人也。
units.en: Xie Yanzhang came from Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: Xie Yanzhang was a native of Xu Prefecture.

units.zh: 幼事葛從周，從周憐其敏惠，養以為子，授之兵法，從周以千錢置大盤中，為行陣偏伍之狀，示以出入進退之節，彥章盡得之。
units.en: As a boy he served Ge Congzhou. Congzhou, taken with his quick wit, raised him as a son and taught him war. He would pour a thousand coins into a broad dish, set them out like columns and squads on the march, and drill the boy in when to advance, halt, and fall back—Yanzhang learned every lesson.
units.literal: In youth he served Ge Congzhou; Congzhou, fond of his keen intelligence, adopted him as a son and taught him the art of war; Congzhou placed a thousand coins in a large tray, arranged them in the formations of marching columns and squads, and showed him the rhythms of advance and retreat—Yanzhang mastered it all.

units.zh: 及壯，事梁太祖為騎將。
units.en: Grown to manhood, he served Taizu of Liang as a cavalry officer.
units.literal: When he came of age he served Taizu of Liang as a cavalry commander.

units.zh: 是時，賀瑰善用步卒，而彥章與孟審澄、侯溫裕皆善將騎兵，審澄、溫裕所將不過三千，彥章多而益辦。
units.en: He Gui then was master of the infantry, while Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng, and Hou Wenyu led the horse. Shencheng and Wenyu each held fewer than three thousand riders; Yanzhang commanded more and ran them tighter.
units.literal: At that time He Gui was skilled with foot soldiers, while Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng, and Hou Wenyu all excelled at leading cavalry; Shencheng and Wenyu commanded no more than three thousand each; Yanzhang had more men and managed them better still.

units.zh: 彥章事末帝，累遷匡國軍節度使。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor he rose step by step to military governor of Kuangguo.
units.literal: Yanzhang served the Last Emperor and was repeatedly promoted to military governor of the Kuangguo army.

units.zh: 貞明四年，晉攻河北，賀瑰為北面招討使，彥章為排陣使，屯於行臺。
units.en: In the fourth year of Zhenming the Jin struck Hebei. He Gui took northern command; Yanzhang served as formation marshal. They camped at the field headquarters.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenming, Jin attacked Hebei; He Gui was northern-route pacification commissioner and Yanzhang formation marshal; they encamped at the field headquarters.

units.zh: 彥章為將，好禮儒士，雖居軍中，嘗儒服，或臨敵禦眾，肅然有將帥之威，左右馳驟，疾若風雨。
units.en: Yanzhang the general honored scholars and often wore plain robes even in camp. Yet when he faced the enemy and held the line, the air of a true commander settled on him; aides riding at his side wheeled as fast as wind and rain.
units.literal: As a commander Yanzhang honored scholars; though he lived in the army he often wore scholar’s robes; yet when he faced the enemy and rallied the host, a general’s stern dignity settled on him; escorts wheeling left and right were swift as wind and rain.

units.zh: 晉人望其行陣齊整，相謂曰：「謝彥章必在此也！」
units.en: Jin lookouts, seeing ranks drawn so tight, told one another: “Xie Yanzhang must be here!”
units.literal: Jin soldiers, seeing ranks so perfectly ordered, said to one another: “Xie Yanzhang must be here!”

units.zh: 其名重敵中如此。
units.en: Such was his name among the foe.
units.literal: His fame among the enemy was weighty to this degree.

units.zh: 瑰心忌之。
units.en: Gui turned jealous.
units.literal: Gui nursed jealousy in his heart.

units.zh: 彥章與瑰行視郊外，瑰指一地語彥章曰：「此地岡阜隆起，其中坦然，營柵之地也。」
units.en: Yanzhang and Gui rode out to survey the countryside. Gui pointed to a spot and said: “The ridge swells here and the hollow inside is flat—ideal ground for a stockade.”
units.literal: Yanzhang and Gui rode out to inspect the outskirts; Gui pointed to a place and told Yanzhang: “Here the hills rise and the center lies open—it is ground for a fortified camp.”

units.zh: 已而晉兵柵之，瑰疑彥章陰以告晉，益惡之。
units.en: Soon the Jin fenced it in. Gui decided Yanzhang had tipped them off in secret and hated him the more.
units.literal: Before long Jin troops palisaded there; Gui suspected Yanzhang had secretly told them and hated him all the more.

units.zh: 彥章故與馬步都虞候朱珪有隙，瑰欲速戰，彥章請持重以老敵，珪乃誣彥章以為將反。
units.en: Yanzhang and Zhu Gui, chief adjutant of horse and foot, had old grievances. Gui wanted a quick fight; Yanzhang pleaded for patience to wear the enemy down. Zhu Gui then accused Yanzhang of plotting rebellion.
units.literal: Yanzhang had long been at odds with the horse-and-foot chief adjutant Zhu Gui; Gui wanted a quick battle; Yanzhang urged patience to wear the enemy down; Zhu Gui then slandered Yanzhang, saying he intended to rebel.

units.zh: 瑰旦享士，使珪伏甲殺之，審澄、溫裕皆見害。
units.en: At dawn Gui feasted his officers and had Zhu Gui hide armed men to cut Yanzhang down; Shencheng and Wenyu were killed too.
units.literal: At dawn Gui feasted his officers and had Zhu Gui lie in ambush with armored men to kill him; Shencheng and Wenyu were killed as well.
